chunks: And it was narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who owes me loads measured by a specified measure, and he sends me loads from them that are less than the measure he owes me, so I take them by estimate without exact measuring. He said: “There is no harm in it.”

He said: And I asked him about a man who has against another one hundred kurr of dates owed to him, and the latter has date-palms. So he comes to him and says: “Give me these date-palms in exchange for what you owe.” It was as though he disliked it.

He said: And I asked him about two men between whom there are date-palms, and one of them says to his companion: “Choose: either you take these date-palms for such-and-such a specified measure and give me half of this measure, whether it increases or decreases, or I take it myself on those terms.” He said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.النَّخْلُ: date-palms involved as property or produce source
key_terms.بِكَيْلٍ مُسَمًّى: a specifically determined measure in a sale or debt
key_terms.كَرِهَهُ: he disliked it or regarded it as disapproved
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no legal objection to it
key_terms.مُجَازَفَةً: taking goods by rough estimate without precise measuring
key_terms.مِائَةُ كُرٍّ: one hundred large measures of produce

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about taking owed goods by estimate and exchanging debts for date-palms?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings related to debts, estimated receipt of measured goods, and transactions involving date-palms and dates. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits accepting less-than-measured loads by estimate in one case and permits a particular arrangement between joint owners, while indicating disapproval toward exchanging owed dates directly for date-palms.
